title: Cross-line attention: MT-LM vs vanilla AR
claim: MT-LM exhibits cross-line attention over previous, current, and later lines. Averaged over ALL heads, its previous/current per-token pattern matches a vanilla AR baseline; the only difference is a small but nonzero later-line component (structurally absent in AR, exactly 0). We are deliberately humble: this is attention allocation, not a causal/functional effect, and the later component is modest on average.
metric: per-token lift = content-attention-share / token-share (1 = proportional to availability; anchors/<sot>/<bos> excluded). Reported as the MEAN over ALL 288 heads (the honest, non-cherry-picked number) and the median head, averaged over docs.
head_specialization_note: The all-head average folds in a minority of specialist heads: later-lift exceeds 1 in only 11% of heads (max 4.8x). We report the average so the headline is not driven by those few heads; the figure uses one such head (L7H5) only to make the mechanism visible.
takeaway: Averaged over all heads: previous and current lifts are similar between MT and AR; later is the difference — MT small-but-nonzero (mean 0.59x), vanilla exactly 0. We do not claim later attention is strong, only that the cross-line channel exists and is exercised where AR's is structurally absent.
